example_question: Why hasn't my shipment moved?
approved_answer: Check the latest tracking scan in your dashboard. If there has been no scan for 48-72 hours after pickup, raise an exception with the shipment ID and last known status. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I track my shipment?
approved_answer: Open Shipments, search the order or AWB number, and view the tracking timeline. The latest scan shows the current location and status. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What does 'in transit' mean?
approved_answer: It means the carrier has picked up or received the shipment and it is moving through the delivery network. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What does 'out for delivery' mean?
approved_answer: The shipment is with the delivery agent and is expected to be delivered on the same day, subject to route and customer availability. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: My tracking has not updated for three days. What should I do?
approved_answer: Raise a delayed-shipment exception with the AWB, last scan, and customer impact. Support will investigate with the carrier. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What happens after a failed delivery?
approved_answer: The carrier usually retries delivery. If repeated attempts fail, the shipment may be returned to origin. Communicate proactively with the customer and update the delivery address if needed. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Customer is unavailable for delivery. What should I do?
approved_answer: Ask the customer to confirm an alternate delivery time or address, then update the shipment instructions before the next attempt. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I raise a delivery exception?
approved_answer: Go to Shipments, select the affected AWB, choose Raise Exception, select the issue type, and add the last tracking update and customer impact. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: My shipment is marked RTO. What does that mean?
approved_answer: RTO means Return to Origin: the shipment could not be delivered and is being returned to the seller's pickup address. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can I stop an RTO after it starts?
approved_answer: In some cases, if the shipment has not been handed back to the seller, support may be able to request a re-attempt. Raise an urgent exception immediately. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: My pickup is delayed. What should I do?
approved_answer: Check the pickup slot and courier assignment. If the pickup window has passed, raise a pickup-delay exception with the order ID and scheduled slot. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I schedule a pickup?
approved_answer: Create or select the shipment, choose Pickup, select an available date and time slot, and confirm the pickup address. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can I change a scheduled pickup?
approved_answer: Yes, before the courier is assigned or arrives. Go to the shipment, select Reschedule Pickup, and choose a new slot. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: The courier did not arrive for pickup. What next?
approved_answer: Raise a missed-pickup exception with the scheduled slot and any courier details. You can also reschedule the pickup. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I initiate a return?
approved_answer: Open the delivered order, select Initiate Return, choose the reason, upload evidence if required, and generate the reverse pickup request. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Who pays for return shipping?
approved_answer: This depends on the return reason and your shipping agreement. Check the return policy shown before confirming the reverse pickup. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can a customer exchange an item instead of returning it?
approved_answer: If exchange is enabled for the catalog item, create an exchange request with the replacement SKU and reason. Otherwise, process a return and create a new order. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: My return pickup has not happened. What should I do?
approved_answer: Check the reverse-pickup slot and courier status. If the slot has passed, raise a return-pickup exception. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Why was my shipping charge adjusted?
approved_answer: Shipping charges can change due to weight revision, dimensions, fuel surcharge, remote-area fee, or a carrier correction. Review the charge breakdown in Billing. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I dispute a shipping charge?
approved_answer: Open Billing, select the transaction, choose Dispute Charge, upload the invoice or proof, and submit the reason. Support reviews disputed charges. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Where can I download invoices?
approved_answer: Go to Billing, select Invoices, choose the period, and download the invoice PDF. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What is COD remittance?
approved_answer: COD remittance is the transfer of cash-on-delivery collections to your registered bank account after applicable deductions. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Why is my COD remittance delayed?
approved_answer: Remittance can be delayed by bank verification, carrier reconciliation, or a compliance hold. Check the remittance status and raise a billing exception if it is overdue. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I add my business details?
approved_answer: Go to Settings, select Business Profile, enter legal business name, address, GST/tax details if applicable, and bank details, then submit for verification. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Why is my business verification pending?
approved_answer: Verification may be pending because documents are unclear, details do not match, or additional proof is required. Check the verification status and re-upload corrected documents. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I add a pickup address?
approved_answer: Go to Settings, select Pickup Addresses, add the complete address with contact details, and verify it before creating shipments. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can I use multiple pickup locations?
approved_answer: Yes. Add each location under Pickup Addresses and select the correct location while creating a shipment. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I create a shipment?
approved_answer: Go to Orders or Shipments, select Create Shipment, enter customer and product details, choose the pickup address and service, then confirm. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can I create shipments in bulk?
approved_answer: Yes. Download the bulk-upload template, fill in the required fields, upload the file, and review validation errors before confirming. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What is an AWB number?
approved_answer: An AWB, or Air Waybill number, is the unique tracking identifier assigned to a shipment by the carrier. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I print a shipping label?
approved_answer: Open the shipment, select Print Label, choose the label format, and print or download the PDF. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: Can I edit a shipment after label generation?
approved_answer: Some fields may be editable before pickup. After the carrier accepts the shipment, changes may require cancellation and recreation. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I reset my password?
approved_answer: Select Forgot Password on the login screen, enter your registered email, and follow the reset link. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I add a team member?
approved_answer: Go to Settings, select Team, choose Invite User, enter their email, assign a role, and send the invitation. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: What roles can team members have?
approved_answer: Common roles include Owner, Admin, Operations, and Finance. Each role has different permissions for orders, billing, and settings. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: How do I update my bank account?
approved_answer: Go to Settings, select Bank Details, enter the new account information, complete verification, and wait for approval before payouts. [HYPOTHETICAL POLICY]

example_question: I lost money because of a delayed shipment. What should I do?
approved_answer: This may require a claim or commercial review. Raise an urgent exception with the AWB, delivery timeline, financial impact, and supporting evidence. [ESCALATE]

example_question: My customer is threatening legal action. What should I do?
approved_answer: Do not provide legal advice. Escalate immediately to support with the shipment ID, customer communication, and incident details. [ESCALATE]

example_question: My account is blocked. What should I do?
approved_answer: Account blocks can involve compliance or risk review. Raise an urgent account-access exception; support will guide you through the required verification. [ESCALATE]

example_question: I suspect fraud on my account. What should I do?
approved_answer: Change your password immediately, review team access, and escalate to support with transaction details and evidence. [ESCALATE]

example_question: My shipment contains restricted items. What should I do?
approved_answer: Restricted-item handling depends on carrier and regulatory rules. Do not ship the item; escalate to support for category-specific guidance. [ESCALATE]

example_question: The carrier says the package was delivered, but the customer says it was not. What should I do?
approved_answer: Raise a delivery-dispute exception with the AWB, delivery proof, customer statement, and any CCTV or address evidence. This may require carrier investigation. [ESCALATE]

example_question: I need a custom API integration for my ERP. What should I do?
approved_answer: API and ERP integration requirements may need technical review. Submit a support request with your ERP, required workflows, and expected order volume. [ESCALATE]

example_question: I want to negotiate custom shipping rates. What should I do?
approved_answer: Custom pricing depends on volume, lanes, and commercial terms. Escalate to the account or sales team with monthly shipment volume and destinations. [ESCALATE]

example_question: My GST details are incorrect and invoices are affected. What should I do?
approved_answer: Tax and invoice corrections can have compliance implications. Raise a billing exception with the invoice numbers and correct GST details. [ESCALATE]

example_question: My shipment is lost. What should I do?
approved_answer: Raise an urgent lost-shipment exception with the AWB, last scan, declared value, invoice, and customer impact. Carrier investigation and claim review may be required. [ESCALATE]
